newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan PM says island row must not hurt Korea ties.
newsitem.headline: Japan PM says island row must not hurt Korea ties.

text.p: Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto said on Tuesday that a territorial dispute between Japan and South Korea over small islands must not jeopardise their bilateral relations.
"Naturally, we have consistently made our position clear," Hashimoto told parliament.
"But the two countries must not confront each other emotionally and damage friendly and cooperative bilateral relations," he said.
Hashimoto made the remarks a day after Tokyo lodged a protest with Seoul over the building of a wharf on the disputed islands in the Sea of Japan, called Takeshima by Japan and Tokdo by South Korea.
"Japan has been consistently asking South Korea to halt the construction work," Hashimoto said.
Asked what action Japan would take if South Korea refused to stop the work, Foreign Ministry spokesman Ken Shimanouchi said: "We can't answer hypothetical questions."
The long-dormant sovereignty dispute was rekindled earlier this year when both sides declared 200-nautical-mile exclusion zones around their coasts, embracing the islands.
The small islands are situated in rich fishing grounds midway between the neighbours.

Tokyo has claimed the islands since 1905 when it signed, some historians say forced, an agreement with Korea that paved the way for Japan's brutal colonial rule over the Korean Peninsula from 1910 to 1945.

Korea says its claim to the islands dates back to 512. Japan established diplomatic relations with South Korea in 1965 but many Koreans still harbour bitter memories of Japan's 35 years of colonial rule.

Hashimoto said he would discuss the islands issue with South Korean President Kim Young-sam when they meet in the hot-spring resort city of Beppu on Japan's southern island of Kyushu on January 25 and 26.
